reading.body:
HVN10 is a 15 MW facility in Trumbull, Connecticut, operated by Aphorio Carter after Digital Realty listed it for sale in 2026. The facility was formerly tracked under Digital Reality ownership and is now confirmed in the DatacenterMap and Inflect registries under its current operator, though the current operator has not published independent specifications for it on their own channels. At 15 MW of IT load, this represents roughly 375 racks at the 40 kW per rack density common in AI training, or roughly 1,500 individual accelerators at 10 kW per GPU, as a baseline assumption.

Connecticut has five mapped data center facilities and publishes confirmed capacity for only two of them, totaling 8 MW. This campus ranks third among published capacity figures in the state, meaning it exceeds the single other facility with a disclosed figure. The published capacity concentrated in only two facilities reflects how sparse transparent power disclosure remains outside the largest metropolitan operator portfolios, even in the Northeast corridor where AI infrastructure has begun to concentrate.

The facility's position outside New Haven and its recent operator transition place it at the margin of visibility in national AI infrastructure planning. Connecticut's total published capacity of 8 MW is negligible in national AI compute terms and sits in a region where major build-out is documented to concentrate in New York City, New Jersey, and northern Virginia instead. This campus contributes materially to understanding the state's footprint, but the lack of published specifications from the current operator and the absence of regional grid context limits any reading of its significance to AI scaling.
